describe_model.title: Describe Model
describe_model.description: Return the complete schema of all entities, attributes, relationships, and enum cases. Call this before any other tool — attribute names are system-specific and cannot be guessed (e.g. isEnabled, not isActive).

fetch.title: Fetch
fetch.description: Fetch entity rows with optional filtering, sorting and pagination. Call once per query — trust the result even if count is 0; do not retry with rephrased predicates.

count.title: Count
count.description: Count entities matching an optional predicate.

aggregate.title: Aggregate
aggregate.description: Compute aggregate values for an entity.

group_by.title: Group By
group_by.description: Group rows and compute aggregates. Call once per query — if rowCount is 0, data is absent; do not retry with different arguments or aliases.

create.title: Create
create.description: Create one entity row, including any related objects nested under `values` (attributes, to-one and to-many relationships, and deeper graphs) in a single call. Use this whenever a row has relationships or nested objects — even when creating several related rows at once. To insert many independent flat rows of the same entity, call it once per row.

delete.title: Delete
delete.description: Delete one existing row. Its related rows follow the deleteRule that describe_model reports on each of its relationships, so check those before deleting: `cascade` deletes the related rows along with this one, in the same call — delete only the parent, never its children first; `nullify` keeps the related rows and only unlinks them; `deny` refuses the deletion while related rows remain, so delete or relink those first; `noAction` does nothing to the related rows — depending on the store the deletion is refused or they are left pointing at a row that no longer exists — so delete or relink them first.

fetch_history.title: Fetch History
fetch_history.description:
Read the Core Data persistent history change log.
Requires exactly one scope marking the boundary history is read after — "afterDate", "afterTransaction" or "afterToken". When more than one is given, precedence is date > transaction > token.
"predicate" further narrows the history in scope, running against "entityName" — PersistentHistoryTransaction by default, or PersistentHistoryChange.
"resultType" is the raw value of PersistentHistoryResultType and shapes what comes back.
Only meaningful when persistent history tracking is enabled for the store.

purge_history.title: Purge History
purge_history.description:
Permanently remove transactions from the Core Data persistent history change log. This is destructive and cannot be undone.
Requires exactly one scope marking the boundary history is removed before — "beforeDate", "beforeTransaction" or "beforeToken". When more than one is given, precedence is date > transaction > token.
"predicate" further narrows which transactions are purged, running against "entityName" — PersistentHistoryTransaction by default, or PersistentHistoryChange.
Only meaningful when persistent history tracking is enabled for the store.

get_server_time.title: Get Server Time
get_server_time.description: Return the server's current date, time and timezone.

web_search.title: Web Search
web_search.description: Search the web using the provider configured by the application.
